communication_expectations: Sofia is 13. Adolescent-appropriate communication is expected: casual but respectful language, building trust before sensitive topics, respecting her autonomy and privacy, and avoiding judgmental or parental tones. She warms up when the interviewer is friendly and shows interest in what she cares about (dance, music).
caregiver_rules: Sofia can speak for herself; parent-framed questions are acceptable for insurance/logistics topics but the student should primarily address Sofia directly and age-appropriately.
patient_goals: Dance again (hip-hop is what she loves most)
Dress herself and manage school without pain

assessment_areas.case_context: Polyarticular JIA (refractory): elbows/wrists 4-6/10 at rest rising to 6-8/10 with dressing or carrying her backpack; left ankle 2/10 rising to 5/10 with stairs, squatting, dancing. Morning patterns and aggravating activities should be explored.
acceptable_approaches: asking what makes it worse or better

assessment_areas.assessment_area: functional impact on daily life and school
assessment_areas.case_context: She is limited in dressing, preparing meals, and schoolwork; the backpack aggravates symptoms; stepping up is impaired.
acceptable_approaches: asking about a typical school day
asking what tasks are hard now
following up on specific limitations she mentions

assessment_areas.assessment_area: dance participation and what it means to her
assessment_areas.case_context: Dance is the thing she loves most and she is currently limited - this is both a functional topic and her core motivation.
acceptable_approaches: exploring what she misses and wants to get back to

assessment_areas.case_context: Her parents report she is 'not herself' and starting to isolate. Sensitive, non-judgmental exploration of mood and social connection is expected once rapport allows.
acceptable_approaches: gentle open questions about how she is doing
asking about friends and what she enjoys

assessment_areas.case_context: A painful, itchy cluster of yellow crusted plaques under her nose (3 days) while on methotrexate and etanercept is a safety-relevant finding: possible infection during immunosuppression deserves exploration or acknowledgment if disclosed.
acceptable_approaches: asking about the sore if visible/mentioned
general screening for new skin changes, fevers, or feeling unwell

assessment_areas.case_context: She takes etanercept and methotrexate; a teenager may know names imperfectly. General medication questions are appropriate.
acceptable_approaches: asking what medicines she takes and how they go
asking about side effects in plain language

assessment_areas.case_context: Insurance is inadequate (deductible met yearly; 20% coinsurance unaffordable for multiple PT visits); transportation and provider access are limited. Relevant if the conversation approaches care planning.
Diet is not well balanced; sleep is good (PAVING sleep 25); daily activity about 30-60 minutes.
Work history and adult occupational demands are not applicable to a 13-year-old student.
